product_family: Filmora AI - AI-powered video editing and content creation platform with 2.9M+ creative assets, available on desktop (Windows/Mac) and mobile (iOS/Android); includes AI features like text-to-video, image-to-video, object removal, auto-caption, and music generation.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on vendor domain. Trust Center page exists but does not list SOC 2 for Filmora or any Wondershare product. (Lumin PDF, which advertises a SOC 2 Type 1 report, is a separate company, not a Wondershare product, and is not evidence for this vendor.)

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on vendor domain for Filmora. Wondershare PDFelement holds ISO 27001 certification, but Filmora does not list this certification.

certifications.name: GDPR
certifications.proof_quote: Implements GDPR-aligned practices (Standard Contractual Clauses for international transfers, EU data residency option) but does not claim formal GDPR certification. Privacy policy states: 'if you are within the European Economic Area, your Personal Data will be processed and stored on the server in EU.'

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on vendor domain. Not a healthcare product; no HIPAA claims or certifications visible.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on vendor domain for Filmora. Wondershare mentions PCI compliance for payment processing in general, but not specific to Filmora product certification.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on vendor domain.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on vendor domain.

privacy.ai_training_note: Wondershare explicitly states: 'We do not use this data to train our own general AI models' and 'we will not use your personal data to research, develop, train and otherwise improve the AI models.' When customer content is sent to third-party AI providers (the vendor's AI privacy page names OpenAI, Azure, Eleven Labs, and PixVerse; the marketing site also cites Google's Veo model), those providers are contractually bound to process data only for service delivery. Biometric data (facial features, voiceprints) from AI features is automatically deleted after generation and not used for identification or shared with third parties.
privacy.data_region: EU data residency available; Standard Contractual Clauses used for international transfers

security.name: Encryption in transit and at rest
security.value: SSL encryption used for payments and data transmission; general encryption for data storage mentioned but specific algorithms not detailed.

security.name: Web Security Verification
security.value: Website verified by SSL Labs and Sucuri; protected by enterprise-grade security services.

security.name: Antivirus Verification
security.value: Software verified by McAfee, Norton, AVG; claims '100% safe, with no virus or malware.'

security.name: Payment Security
security.value: Payment data secured by SecureTrust with advanced encryption technology.

security.name: Data Protection
security.value: Implements technical and organizational security measures to protect against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, or unauthorized disclosure.

products.name: Filmora Desktop
products.data_scope: Local video files, project data, account information; AI features send content to third-party providers with consent
products.notes: Available on Windows and Mac; supports 2.9M+ creative assets; core timeline and rendering work offline; advanced AI features require internet

products.name: Filmora Mobile
products.data_scope: Local video files on device, account information; AI features require cloud processing
products.notes: Available on iOS and Android; subset of desktop features; cloud storage for projects optional

products.name: Filmora AI Text-to-Video
products.data_scope: Text prompts sent to Google/OpenAI servers; generated video stored locally by default
products.notes: Uses Gemini 3.0 or OpenAI API; requires explicit user consent before processing

products.name: Filmora AI Image/Video Processing
products.data_scope: Images and video frames sent to Google (Veo 3.0/3.1), OpenAI (Sora 2), or Kuaishou (Kling 2.5) servers; results returned to user
products.notes: Biometric data (faces, voices) automatically deleted after processing; not retained by Wondershare or providers

compare.pricing_model: Freemium (free tier with watermark) + subscription plans (monthly, yearly, lifetime)
compare.data_residency: EU data residency available for GDPR compliance; data transfers to US-based AI providers (Google, OpenAI) with consent
top_certs: No formal certifications held by Filmora product itself
Parent company (Wondershare) does not publicly list formal SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA certifications for Filmora
PDFelement product (different Wondershare offering) holds ISO 27001; not applicable to Filmora

flags: No vendor-domain source explicitly lists formal security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP) for Filmora. Trust Center page exists but does not detail specific certifications.
Product-level certifications vs. parent-company certifications unclear: Wondershare PDFelement has ISO 27001, but not Filmora.
Earlier Filmora versions (12.x, 13.x, 14.5.16) had local privilege escalation CVEs; recommend checking current version (15.x) patch status.

AI training policy is clear and positive (no self-training on customer data), but relies on third-party AI providers' compliance (Google, OpenAI, Kuaishou); user consent required for data transmission.
GDPR compliance is implemented (Standard Contractual Clauses, EU data residency) but not formally certified.
Biometric data handling is transparent (auto-deletion post-processing) but not formally audited or certified.
